sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a decelerating growth curve: 64.2% in FY2021, 11.8% in FY2022, 0.1% in FY2023, then 16.4% and 10.6% in FY2024 and FY2025 [D218][D263][D311][D358][D406].
The FY2017 operating loss of $3,485.6 million reflected a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the CEO award and IPO-related RSUs [F12][P74].
The FY2022 loss widened to $1,395.3 million on higher cost of revenue and operating expenses, partly offset by revenue growth [F17][P42].
The operating loss has narrowed every year since FY2022, to $532.2 million in FY2025, a margin of -9.0% against a window median of -32.4% [F20][F30][D555].
North America remains the largest market at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D456][D458][D406].
Other revenue, at 12.6% of FY2025 revenue, grew 62.9% and contributed 5.4pp, nearly matching advertising's 5.3pp [D543][D544][D545][D538].

Advertising revenue rose on roughly 17% more impressions, largely from Sponsored Snaps and Spotlight, partly offset by a 10% lower cost per impression; other revenue grew on subscription growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth in FY2025, an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D423][D406][D429].
The diluted share count rose 2.1% in FY2025 while the net loss fell 34.0%, so the loss per share fell 35.7% [D425][D408][D410].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a median of -32.4% and a low of -422.5% in FY2017 [F30][D554][D555][D553].
Of the 5.7pp margin improvement in FY2025, cost of revenue added 1.1pp, R&D 1.3pp and other lines 3.3pp [D419][D431][D432][D433].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events, lower advertising, and $19.9 million of prior-year restructuring charges [P22].
R&D rose $101.9 million on product development and headcount, partly offset by $38.8 million of prior-year restructuring charges [P23].
Net margin of -7.8% sits 1.2pp above operating margin, with the gap held down by $122.0 million of interest expense against $68.9 million of other income [F50][F30][D591][X100][X130].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million exceeded the $460.5 million net loss in FY2025, and free cash flow was $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin [F80][F40][F100][D393].
Operating cash flow rose on the net loss adjusted for $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of D&A, plus working-capital timing [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, up from a 0.59x ratio in FY2021 [F90][D392][D395][D207].
Capex in both years was primarily improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces [P10].

Net cash swung from $1,439.8 million in FY2021 to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, -10.1% of revenue and the 0th percentile against internet peers whose median is 45.0% [D211][D399][D400][D578][D579].
In February 2025 the company issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of 2026-2028 notes, producing a $66.9 million gain [P1][P2].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow in FY2025, the third straight year above 100% [D401][D402][D307][D354].
The current ratio fell to 3.56x, the window low, from a 5.15x median [F180][D565][D567].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of FY2025 revenue and has been at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390][D22][D66].
Net cash has fallen four years running into net debt, from $1,439.8 million in FY2021 to -$596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D211][D399].
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at 544.3%, 142.3% and 171.7% [R4][D307][D354][D402].
Operating margin: a FY2026 reading above the FY2025 high of -9.0% would confirm the narrowing trend, while a move back toward the -32.4% median would reverse it [F30][D554][D555].
Net cash: a return above zero, from -$596.3 million in FY2025, would reverse the four-year slide into net debt [D399][D211].
Free cash flow margin: holding above the FY2025 high of 7.4% would confirm the cash trend; falling back toward the -4.1% median would not [D560][D561].
